newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares finished well down after directionless trade on Thursday as profit-taking and some negativity from disappointing results knocked prices, dealers said.
Golds also ended weaker on the back of a dull bullion price, which failed to hold the gains the yellow metal made earlier this week.
"All around it's been a relatively weak day for the South African market," one dealer said.
"I think general sentiment has been down, we also had a weaker bullion price failing to follow through and investors did not have much belief in this gold price," one dealer said.
The industrial index closed down 53.3 points at 8,440.6, and the gold index down 15.4 points at 1,254.7 and the all-share down 41.4 points at 7,173.1.
Dealers said among stocks with rekindled interest on the market had been New Africa Investment (Nail), Driefontein and Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd (GFSA).
Nail, the black empowerment group headed by former African National Congress secretary-general Cyril Ramaphosa, said it planned to buy a stake in Gold Fields, the world's third largest gold producer.
It said the buy would give it an effective 17.2 percent stake in the mining house.

"Yes definitely, these shares have been the highlight of the day on the back of the deal.It's still early days at the moment, there is nothing confirmed but the marcet perhaps perceives this to be positive," one dealer said.
Nail is in talks with Driefontein Consolidated Ltd which holds a 40 percent stake in Gold Fields, through its shareholding in Asteroid Ltd.
"Driefontein and Gold Fields have been some of the only gold stocks rising up today," one dealer added.
Gold Fields finished up 825 cents at 118.00 rand, Dries up 85 cents at 41.60 rand and Nail up 35 cents at 425 cents.

Other features were timber and pulp concern Sappi, which added 10 cents to 39.60 following a foreign trade and a bookover deal, both involving a total of about one million shares, worth around 40 million rand.
First National Bank closed up 95 cents at 35.00 rand with over a million shares changing hands on the stock.

Dealers said they expect Friday's trade to be dreary and awaited no cue from the Dow as Wall Street was busy digesting a slew of U.S. economic data giving ambigious interest rate clues. "Certainly our market hasn't been tracking the Dow in the last couple of days. So we are more likely to look at our bonds and our rand and also bullion. It has been a very big sentiment driver for South African shares," a dealer said.
South African near-dated gold share futures also tracked bullion to end weaker, dealers said.
The June gold contracts were last at 878/85 from the 890 settlement, industrial contracts were at 8,240/45 from 8,298 and the all-share at 6,600/10 from 6,643.
